nodes.title: Never hand-write prompts; build an LLM prompt generator per model

verbatim.quote: we're going to leverage this dense 38-page C Dance 2.5 guide... We're going to let ChatGPT do everything for us
would you like a V2 cinematic upgrade with more advanced Hollywood-level camera direction

nodes.interpretation: Standing workflow: paste the model's official guide into ChatGPT/Claude, ask for a reusable prompt generator, iterate with a 'V2 cinematic upgrade' pass. Our pipeline instance: Seedance 2.5 guide + this graph loaded into a Claude project as the video team's prompt engineer.

nodes.title: Seedance 2.5 structured prompt rules

verbatim.quote: when it comes to AI video, specifically C Dance 2.5, structure matters. Timestamps, character lock, global lock, one camera movement per scene and shot. You don't want to have multiple camera movements in one paragraph. If you do, split it up in different timestamps

anything you want a global lock for, i.e. a character, tag that in the very beginning, global lock, and then tag your image. And so the next thing when it comes to timestamps, this is perhaps the most crucial part

nodes.interpretation: Timestamps per shot block; GLOBAL LOCK (character + reference image) tagged first; character lock per scene; one camera movement per block; long structured beats short clever. Re-author our Seedance b-roll/demo scenes to this.

nodes.title: Reference-image stacks drive consistency and product placement

verbatim.quote: how to structure a 50 input reference stack. Now, that's one of the things C-Dance does. You can upload up to 50 images
What are we going to tag as the product being referenced? In this case, let's go with my specific energy drin

nodes.interpretation: Seedance accepts up to 50 reference images; tag character AND product references. Yappyverse 16-image character packs are ready-made reference sets (Watcher visual pass, pattern 1). This is the mechanism behind AI product placement (Watcher pattern 4).

nodes.title: Write prompts like a filmmaker to pass moderation

verbatim.quote: a prompt that reads like a filmmaker describing a shot tends to pass. A prompt that reads like a note to a friend, that tends to get flagged
real faces of identifiable people... celebrities, politicians, and public figures... named copyright or trademarked items

nodes.interpretation: Seedance LLM-reads whole prompts. Pre-flight rule for client spots: production language only, no identifiable real faces, no trademarked IP.

nodes.title: Veo 3.1 five-part prompt formula
nodes.interpretation: [Camera movement + lens] -> [Subject + physics/secondary motion] -> [Lighting + atmosphere] -> [Layered audio: foreground/mid/background] -> [Technical tokens: 8k, temporal coherence, photorealistic, cinematic color grading].

nodes.title: Kling 3.0 director-style multi-shot formula
nodes.interpretation: Subject + Action + Setting + Camera + Style in explicit shot language; native multi-shot storyboards [Shot 1]-[Shot 6]; native audio/dialogue cues ('Man speaks: ...').

nodes.title: Captured, not created - the realism doctrine
nodes.interpretation: Named camera systems (ARRI ALEXA 35/Mini LF, RED V-RAPTOR 8K), cinema lenses, explicit focal length + aperture, preserved grain/imperfect focus, physically motivated lighting, genre-adaptive token sets. Modes: MOVIE_SET vs STILLS_ARCHIVE. Plastic skin/glow/CGI sharpness = fail. This is the gauntlet Realism axis externalized.

nodes.interpretation: Feed a viral video/screenshot to the LLM, reverse the prompt, apply the V2 cinematic upgrade. Use for competitor ad teardowns and the gauntlet calibration set.
